jobs.name: grocery-receipt-pull-sunday
jobs.prompt:
Grocery Receipt Pull — Sunday Night

You need to pull grocery receipt data from Harris Teeter and Sam's Club for the past week.

IMPORTANT: Send Ted a message first asking him to make sure the browser is active and logged in to both stores. Say: "Sunday night grocery pull — make sure you're logged in to Harris Teeter and Sam's Club in the browser, then I'll extract new receipts."

After notifying Ted, proceed if the session is active.

READ ONE RECEIPT, WRITE IT, THEN NEXT — never hold the week in your head or your output:
For EACH new order: extract that receipt's items, IMMEDIATELY append its rows to the ledger, then move to the next order. Keep every single response small — a few tool calls plus at most one receipt's worth of ledger rows. Never emit multiple receipts' rows in one go, and never emit rows for a receipt you have not yet appended. If a response is getting long, stop and append what you have before extracting more. A mid-run failure must cost at most one receipt, never the week.

Steps for Harris Teeter:
1. Navigate to https://www.harristeeter.com/mypurchases
2. Check for orders since the last entry in /Volumes/Extra/Substrate/Commons/Substrate_Finance_Planning/27_Grocery_Item_Ledger.md
3. For each new order: read its detail page, append that order's rows to the ledger, then open the next order

Steps for Sam's Club (PRINT VIEW method - most reliable):
1. Navigate to https://www.samsclub.com/orders
2. Check for orders since the last Sam's Club entry in the ledger
3. For each new order:
   a. Click "View details" button
   b. Click "Print receipt" button (print-optimized view, all items visible)
   c. Extract items from DOM: select .print-items-list .flex.justify-between elements
   d. Parse: name is text before "Qty", qty is from "Qty N" pattern, price is the last $XX.XX in the text
   e. Append that order's rows to the ledger NOW, before opening the next order
4. The print view also shows fees: .print-fees-item elements contain "Pickup FREE", "Tax $X.XX"

Ledger: /Volumes/Extra/Substrate/Commons/Substrate_Finance_Planning/27_Grocery_Item_Ledger.md
Row format (existing):
|| Date | Store | Receipt | Item raw | Item normalized | Group | Qty | Unit | Paid | Confidence | Notes |

The ledger's last entry is your resume point — only pull orders newer than it, so if a run dies partway, the next run picks up exactly where it left off.

jobs.name: shopping-guru-wednesday-checkin
jobs.prompt:
Weekly Shopping Guru check-in for Ted. This is a conversation, not a report — keep it brief and natural, like a text from a friend.

Ted's approach: flexible shopper who aims to get every item on sale. Will pivot based on what's on deal. Two hard no's: shrimp (severe allergy), mayo (won't eat it). Lives alone, so bulk awareness matters.

STEP 1 — LIVE DEAL PULL (do this FIRST, before writing anything):
- Use the ht-grocery skill patterns. Ensure the CDP browser is up: Chrome at /Volumes/Extra/Apps/Google Chrome.app with --remote-debugging-port=9223 --user-data-dir="/Users/ted/Library/Application Support/Google/Chrome/Cost Tabs" --remote-allow-origins='*' (Chrome 152+ needs the origins flag).
- Pull the weekly ad live (nav to Save > Weekly Ad, or the /specials/weeklyad li-scan pattern from the skill).
- Save the verified result to /Volumes/Extra/Substrate/Commons/Substrate_Finance_Planning/Evidence/Grocery_Receipt_Staging/ht_deals_weeklyad_latest.json (plus a dated copy). This replaces the retired scraper script.
- Verify deal_count > 0 before continuing. If the pull fails after 2-3 pattern variations from the skill, STOP the pull, say so plainly in your message, and still send the check-in — do not fabricate deals.

STEP 2 — DEAL SELECTION (Ted's priority order):
1. BOGO / Buy-One-Get-One and B2G2/B2G3 deals first — these are his favorite savings.
2. Half-price and multi-buy (e.g. 5/$5) deals next.
3. Substantial single-item markdowns (roughly 30%+ off or a striking price like sweet corn at 33c/ear).
Focus on things Ted actually eats: chicken (wings, thighs — air fryer meal prep), salad fixings (spinach/spring mix, feta, olives, sundried tomatoes, kalamatas), pantry staples (heavy cream, chicken broth, canned fruit), gala apples, corn in season, bacon when on sale, Birds Eye frozen sides, dark chocolate.

STEP 3 — MATCH AGAINST PURCHASE HISTORY (in your head, not via script):
Read Ted's recent purchases from the receipt ledger in the same Grocery_Receipt_Staging folder and cross-reference: which of this week's BOGO/sale items are things he actually buys? Those go first. Ignore one-off match noise; never recommend shrimp or mayo.

STEP 4 — MESSAGE:
Flag the best 2-3 deals worth his attention, leading with BOGOs. Note fuel points coupons to clip. Mention bulk-too-big-for-one-person flags. Don't over-explain — a quick "here's what I see this week" is perfect.
